Chokepoint Watch: Memory and Packaging
Supply-chain research · weekly · evidence, not a trade

Chokepoint Watch: Memory and Packaging

As of 2026-10-19 Edition 1 Previous edition first edition
Changed
First edition. No earlier edition was found among the user's artifacts. The board opens with 3 chokepoints (2 deep-dived) and 6 rejected candidates.
Top
mem-1, DRAM wafer capacity behind HBM. Micron says the industry will "remain supply constrained" in both 2027 and 2028, and new cleanroom space is the binding term.
Next dated
Besi Q3 (22 Oct), Advantest and FormFactor (28 Oct), Samsung 3Q call (29 Oct), SK hynix 3Q (late Oct; date not confirmed).
Evidence marks: primaryleadmapcontradictedunexamined

Predictions settled this week

None. This is the first edition, so no predictions have come due.

The board

mem-1

DRAM wafer capacity (cleanroom-bound) feeding HBM

layer: waferdeep-divestatus: new

Chain

  • mapAI accelerators need HBM3E/HBM4 stacks beside the GPU or ASIC
  • mapEach HBM stack is built from DRAM core dies cut from DRAM wafers, which use more wafer area per bit than conventional DRAM
  • PDRAM wafer output is limited by cleanroom space. Micron says cleanroom additions are needed to close the gap.
  • PConstrained layer: DRAM wafer starts at the three makers. Micron and Samsung both say supply is short.

Six steps

StepStateEvidence
ConstraintprimaryIndustry DRAM bits, at the wafer layer. Unit: bits; Micron gives growth rates, not wafer counts.
"For calendar 2027 and 2028, we expect industry DRAM bit shipments to grow approximately in the low-20s percentage range and the industry to remain supply constrained in both years."Micron, FQ4 2026 prepared remarks, 2026-09-30
Demand vs supplyprimary
"Even with additional industry DRAM cleanroom space plans, with robust demand trends including new upside requests from customers, we do not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance."Micron, 2026-09-30
"서버향 DRAM, Enterprise SSD 및 HBM 수요 성장가속화로 인해 공급 부족 현상은 지속될 전망" [Supply shortage expected to continue as server DRAM, enterprise SSD and HBM demand growth accelerates.]Samsung Electronics, 2Q 2026 earnings presentation, July 2026
ReliefprimaryNew cleanroom space, which arrives from mid-2027 and mostly in late 2028. Output also ramps a few quarters after first wafers.
"Our ID1 fab is on track to commence wafer output in mid-calendar 2027, and ID2 is on track to commence wafer output in late calendar 2028."Micron, 2026-09-30
"The structural gap between DRAM supply and demand growth rates is resulting in ongoing supply tightness, and cleanroom additions are required to augment node-transition supply growth and help narrow the gap."Micron, 2026-09-30
ControlmapSK hynix, Samsung and Micron hold almost all HBM-qualified DRAM capacity. Shares were not verified from primary sources this week, and SK hynix documents could not be reached.
CaptureprimaryThe makers book the economics through price, and HBM is now repriced toward conventional DRAM.
"We have completed agreements for the vast majority of our calendar 2027 HBM bit supply with significant price increases year over year, narrowing the gross margin gap with conventional DRAM."Micron, 2026-09-30
"Consolidated gross margin for fiscal Q4 was 87.0%, up 210 basis points sequentially."Micron, 2026-09-30 (non-GAAP; GAAP 86.8% per press-release table)
InvalidationleadMicron guides a slower price rise. No maker has said the shortage is easing.
"We expect higher gross margins beyond fiscal Q1 for the remainder of fiscal 2027, with a more moderate rate of price increases."Micron, 2026-09-30

Physical scarcity

SupportedTwo makers' primary documents. The horizon runs through 2028.

Economic capture

Supported (Micron)87% gross margin; 2027 HBM contracted at higher prices. Samsung and SK hynix capture was not examined.

Investability

Listed, unexaminedAll three holders are listed. Dilution and the export-control exposure of China fabs were not examined.

Bear checks

Dilutionunexamined No equity raise seen. Capex rises in FY2027 ("approximately $25 billion" in 1H FY27), so funding was not checked.
GAAP marginsprimary Micron GAAP gross margin was 86.8% in FQ4 2026.
Customer concentrationunexamined HBM sells to a few accelerator vendors. Micron cites 26 long-term agreements (SCAs) and about $150B RPO, which cuts both ways.
Cash vs debtunexamined
Second sourcemap There are already three sources. The risk is a fourth entrant (China's CXMT), which would mainly serve domestic demand. Not checked.
Bypass architecturemap No HBM substitute exists within 24 months. Custom base dies move the logic die to foundries (Samsung Foundry sells "HBM Base Die", P), but the DRAM core dies stay.
Pull-forward / inventorylead "New upside requests from customers" could include double ordering. No inventory data was checked.
Memory-cycle reversalprimary Price increases are slowing ("more moderate rate"), and this is the main watch item.
Policy reversalunexamined
Layer errorlead Micron's statements cover DRAM bits overall (wafer layer), not HBM stacking. Only the contract statement is HBM-specific, and being contracted is not the same as being short.

Kill criteria

  • Any of the three makers says in an earnings release or call that DRAM supply and demand have returned to balance, or that it expects them to before end-2027.
  • A maker reports a quarter-on-quarter fall in DRAM average selling price, or reports customer inventory builds, in its own results.
  • Micron's FQ1 2027 results (Dec 2026) withdraw the "supply constrained in both years" language.

Predictions

mem-p1 · By 2027-04-15, Micron's fiscal Q2 2027 earnings prepared remarks will still describe the industry DRAM market as supply-constrained in calendar 2027 and will not say supply and demand have returned to balance, as shown by Micron's earnings prepared remarks.
mem-p2 · By 2027-01-15, Micron's fiscal Q1 2027 results will report a non-GAAP consolidated gross margin of at least 84%, as shown by Micron's earnings press release.

Status since last edition: new.

mem-2

CoWoS-class 2.5D back-end and silicon interposer at TSMC

layer: interposer / packagedeep-divestatus: new

Chain

  • mapAccelerator logic die and HBM stacks sit side by side on a 2.5D package
  • PCoWoS is the leading 2.5D option, and TSMC alone ships 5x-reticle packages
  • PTSMC admits a back-end shortage and has contracted GlobalFoundries for silicon interposers
  • PConstrained layer: silicon interposer and CoWoS back-end at TSMC. The interposer is named by GF; "back end" is TSMC's own coarse term.

Six steps

StepStateEvidence
ConstraintprimaryTSMC says there is a back-end shortage and ties GF to it. No unit (wafers per month) was given.
"Definitely, we have a little bit shortage on the back end, and we'd like to work with our so-called partner with GlobalFoundries so that both TSMC and GlobalFoundries can support TSMC's customers for their product to be introduced with enough support and the capacity."C.C. Wei, TSMC 3Q26 earnings call, 2026-10-15
Demand vs supplyleadWei's demand-gap statement is not specific to packaging, so it supports no packaging step on its own.
"And I want to emphasize again - in our judgment, we consider all the parameters, and the demand actually is still far above our capability today to supply."C.C. Wei, 2026-10-15
ReliefprimaryA second US interposer source at GF Malta arrives in 1H 2028, outside most of the horizon. CoPoS (panel) is in development.
"Volume production is expected to begin ramping at GF's Malta site during the first half of 2028."GlobalFoundries press release, 2026-10-08
"Of course, we are also working on the CoPoS part and to make sure that in the future, we can offer a reasonable cost reduction."C.C. Wei, 2026-10-15
ControlprimaryTSMC claims it is the only producer at 5x reticle. No share figure was given.
"Still, I want to say that today's situation, we are the only one that makes sure that the advanced packaging is a 5x reticle size."C.C. Wei, 2026-10-15
CaptureunexaminedTSMC gave no packaging revenue share or margin on the call. GF earns a manufacturing fee under a "Multi-year $2 billion agreement" (GF, 2026-10-08).
InvalidationprimaryTSMC calls the shortage "a little bit", and says rivals are competitive.
"As time goes by, yes, our competitors offer a very competitive solution."C.C. Wei, 2026-10-15

Physical scarcity

Supported, mild wordingThe holder admits it, but calls it "a little bit". No capacity unit was given.

Economic capture

UnprovenTSMC does not report packaging economics separately.

Investability

Listed holderTSMC is listed. The relief entrant, GF, is listed. Export-control exposure was not examined.

Bear checks

Dilutionunexamined CapEx 2026–28 "significantly higher than the past three years" (Huang).
GAAP marginsunexamined Packaging margin is not disclosed.
Customer concentrationmap A few AI accelerator vendors take most CoWoS.
Cash vs debtunexamined
Second sourceprimary GF Malta interposers from 1H 2028. Rivals are "very competitive" (Wei). Intel EMIB-class and OSAT 2.5D were not checked.
Bypass architectureprimary CoPoS (panel-level) is in TSMC's own pipeline. No date was given.
Pull-forward / inventoryunexamined
Memory-cycle reversalmap Not directly linked. A slip in HBM supply would idle CoWoS slots.
Policy reversalunexamined
Layer errorlead "Back end" could mean interposer, CoW bonding, or substrate attach. Only the GF release names the interposer layer.

Kill criteria

  • A TSMC earnings call (next: 4Q26, mid-January 2027) says advanced packaging or back-end capacity now meets demand.
  • An accelerator vendor's 10-Q/10-K drops packaging capacity as a named supply constraint.
  • A non-TSMC 2.5D line at 5x reticle or larger enters volume for a top-3 accelerator before mid-2027, per that company's own release.

Prediction

mem-p3 · By 2027-01-31, TSMC's 4Q26 earnings call transcript will contain an executive statement that advanced-packaging or back-end supply is still short of, or tight against, customer demand, as shown by TSMC's earnings call transcript.

Status since last edition: new.

mem-3

Low-CTE glass cloth (T-glass) for ABF/BT substrate cores

layer: materiallead-ranked, not deep-divedstatus: new

Chain

  • mapLarge CoWoS-class packages sit on large ABF substrates that must not warp
  • mapSubstrate cores use low-thermal-expansion glass cloth to control warpage
  • LNittobo is said to supply most low-CTE cloth, and trade press calls it short
  • PNittobo's mid-term plan pushes further special-glass capacity investment (undated page; T-glass is not named)

Six steps

StepStateEvidence
ConstraintleadTrendForce and others describe a T-glass shortage. No primary text was read.
Demand vs supplyleadPostation (2026-09-21) says Nittobo plans to double T-glass capacity by FY2027 and start a Fukushima building in FY2026 Q4. Not verified in a Nittobo document.
ReliefprimaryNittobo is investing in capacity; timing came from leads only.
"将来を見据え、国内外でスペシャルガラスの更なる増産投資を推進" [Looking ahead, push further capacity investment in special glass in Japan and abroad.]Nittobo, Medium-term Management Plan page (undated), nittobo.co.jp/ir/keiei/chukei.htm
ControlleadTrade press says Nittobo holds roughly 90% share. Taiwanese competitors are in customer qualification (lead).
CaptureleadPostation reports earlier price rises, then no further hikes (attributed to a 2026-05-12 Q&A).
InvalidationleadCustomers are reported to be evaluating other low-CTE glass. A no-more-price-hikes stance weakens capture.

Physical scarcity

Lead onlyRanked high by trade press. No primary support this week.

Economic capture

Lead onlyThe holder reportedly chose share over price.

Investability

Listed (TSE 3110)Not examined further.

Kill criteria

  • Nittobo's own results materials say low-CTE supply now meets demand.
  • A substrate maker (Ibiden, Unimicron and others) or a rival weaver announces volume qualification of a second low-CTE cloth for AI substrates.
  • No primary support is found within two more editions. Move it to Rejected.

Prediction

mem-p4 · By 2027-02-28, Nittobo's 3Q FY2026 results materials will state that its new special-glass capacity at Fukushima is on schedule to start production by end-March 2027, as shown by Nittobo's results presentation or Q&A summary.

Status since last edition: new.

Rejected

CandidateReason
HBM TC bondersSeveral vendors, and orders are timed to customer launches, not tool supply.
"In memory, even as the Group continued to secure repeat orders from HBM manufacturers, the timing of customers' new tool purchase decisions remains dependent on HBM4 product rollout schedules."ASMPT, 2026 interim results, 2026-07-29
Hybrid bonders for HBMNot yet qualified for HBM volume, so not binding inside the horizon.
"Active collaboration with key logic and memory customers has progressed to the sampling stage, an important step toward potential qualification."ASMPT, 2026-07-29
Besi cites hybrid-bonding order strength (2026-07-23) but names no HBM qualification. Reopen when HBM4E or HBM5 adopts it.
Memory / HBM testersCapacity is expanding, and the leader expects to lose memory share, so alternatives exist.
"On the memory tester side, expansion plans are progressing in parallel with SoC tester capacity expansion."Advantest, Q1 FY2026 Q&A, 2026-07-29
Reopen after the 28 Oct results.
NAND / enterprise SSDShort (Micron: "the industry to remain supply constrained in both years", 2026-09-30), but five or more qualified suppliers share it. This is industry-wide tightness, not a single-control chokepoint. Held on watch.
HBM logic base dieAt least two foundry sources. Samsung Foundry cites "HBM Base Die" demand (Samsung 2Q26 presentation, July 2026); TSMC is the other (map).
ABF substrate capacityNot ranked. Ibiden and Unimicron primary pages could not be read (JavaScript lists, robots block). Reopen when they can be.

Cross-theme hooks

  • Low-CTE glass cloth is shared by IC substrates and high-layer-count AI server PCBs (lead). Both themes compete for one weaver's output.
  • Test capacity: Advantest now plans on 18-month forecasts "because of the scale of the industry and the constraints in advanced packaging and wafer starts" (P, 2026-07-29). The same SoC testers serve all AI logic.
  • Power: TSMC's CEO named "power supply situation" as a factor in his demand assessment (P, 2026-10-15). Data-center power caps how much accelerator and HBM demand turns into shipments.

Next questions

  • Does SK hynix's 3Q26 release say 2027 HBM is sold out, and when does M15X add wafers? Look at the SK hynix IR PDF or a call transcript; the newsroom refused fetches this week.
  • Does Samsung's 3Q26 call (29 Oct) give an end date for the DRAM shortage, or base-die volumes? Look at the Samsung IR conference-call materials.
  • Do Advantest's and FormFactor's results (28 Oct) report HBM test or probe-card lead times? Look at their earnings releases and Q&A.
  • Does Besi's Q3 (22 Oct) name an HBM hybrid-bonding qualification? Look at the Besi press release.
  • Do Nittobo's 2Q FY2026 results (early Nov) confirm T-glass capacity doubling and Fukushima timing in its own words? Look at the Nittobo IR PDF; this needs a direct PDF link.

Run notes

  • Step 0: The artifact list (64 items) held no "Chokepoint Watch" artifact. No past-chat search tool was available. This is edition 1, and no prior content was assumed.
  • Unreachable: SK hynix newsroom and IR (fetch errors), Unimicron (robots), the Ibiden and Nittobo IR document lists (rendered by JavaScript), the Besi half-year PDF (robots) and FormFactor's Q2 release.
  • Unverified: all Nittobo capacity and price claims (trade press only), vendor shares, and Unimicron's September revenue.
  • Method: Primary quotes were read verbatim in this run by fetch sub-agents from the URLs listed in the ledger. Samsung quotes are Korean originals with my translations.
  • Tool calls: about 25 top-level calls and about 53 page fetches inside sub-agents, roughly 78 in total.
